To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nm23 gene expression is widespread during mouse embryogenesis and is associated with epithelial cell differentiation.
Nm23 is expressed in embryonic tissues, and that Nm23 levels increase with the differentiation of embryonic tissues.

nm23 is expressed throughout mouse embryonic development, that the amount of N23 protein is low at the onset of development, that the protein begins to increase in amount in the developing nervous and cardiac systems, that the protein increases in amount as epithelial tissues begin to differentiate, that the increase in protein amount is transient in intestinal tissue and cyclic in mammary tissue during lactation, and that the protein remains at high levels in most tissues into adult life.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the nm23 gene product in the regulation of cell migration and differentiation.
the molecular and cellular biology of the nonmetastatic (Nm23) protein.
the role of the nm23-H1 gene product in the development of the nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Nm23 expression is associated with epithelial differentiation in a variety of embryonic and adult organs, and that this expression may be related to the differentiation state of epithelial cells.

Nm23 expression in the mouse embryo is associated with the differentiation of multiple tissues, but not with cell proliferation, and that this pattern of expression is maintained in the adult mouse, although in some tissues, Nm23 expression is transient.

the nm23 gene expression is not only associated with the development of the mouse embryo but also with the functional differentiation and maturation of multiple epithelial cell types during mouse organogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nm23 gene product is expressed in a wide variety of normal and neoplastic cells.
Nm23 is a developmentally regulated gene whose expression is correlated with differentiation of epithelial cells in multiple organs.
Nm23 is expressed in the developing mouse embryo in a pattern that is consistent with its role in cell motility and differentiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of the nm23 gene in the mouse embryo is widespread and dynamic, with high expression in tissues that are actively differentiating.
Nm23 expression is not restricted to the adult but rather is expressed during embryonic development and in the adult in a tissue-specific manner.
the expression of Nm23 is a marker of epithelial tissue differentiation during mouse embryogenesis.
